functions.name: GOVERN
functions.description: The organization's cybersecurity risk management strategy, expectations, and policy are established, communicated, and monitored

functions.name: IDENTIFY
functions.description: The organization's current cybersecurity risks are understood

functions.name: PROTECT
functions.description: Safeguards to manage the organization's cybersecurity risks are used

functions.name: DETECT
functions.description: Possible cybersecurity attacks and compromises are found and analyzed

functions.name: RESPOND
functions.description: Actions regarding a detected cybersecurity incident are taken

functions.name: RECOVER
functions.description: Assets and operations affected by a cybersecurity incident are restored

categories.name: Organizational Context
categories.description: The circumstances — mission, stakeholder expectations, dependencies, and legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements — surrounding the organization's cybersecurity risk management decisions are understood

categories.name: Risk Management Strategy
categories.description: The organization's priorities, constraints, risk tolerance and appetite statements, and assumptions are established, communicated, and used to support operational risk decisions

categories.name: Roles Responsibilities and Authorities
categories.description: Cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and authorities to foster accountability, performance assessment, and continuous improvement are established and communicated

categories.name: Policy
categories.description: Organizational cybersecurity policy is established, communicated, and enforced

categories.name: Oversight
categories.description: Results of organization-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance are used to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy

categories.name: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management
categories.description: Cyber supply chain risk management processes are identified, established, managed, monitored, and improved by organizational stakeholders

categories.name: Asset Management
categories.description: Assets (e.g., data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organization to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organizational objectives and the organization's risk strategy

categories.name: Risk Assessment
categories.description: The cybersecurity risk to the organization, assets, and individuals is understood by the organization

categories.name: Improvement
categories.description: Improvements to organizational cybersecurity risk management processes, procedures, and activities are identified across all CSF Functions

categories.name: Identity Management Authentication and Access Control
categories.description: Access to physical and logical assets is limited to authorized users, services, and hardware and managed commensurate with the assessed risk of unauthorized access

categories.name: Awareness and Training
categories.description: The organization's personnel are provided cybersecurity awareness and training so that they can perform their cybersecurity-related tasks

categories.name: Data Security
categories.description: Data are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information

categories.name: Platform Security
categories.description: The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organization's risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and availability

categories.name: Technology Infrastructure Resilience
categories.description: Security architectures are managed with the organization's risk strategy to protect asset confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and organizational resilience

categories.name: Continuous Monitoring
categories.description: Assets are monitored to find anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events

categories.name: Adverse Event Analysis
categories.description: Anomalies, indicators of compromise, and other potentially adverse events are analyzed to characterize the events and detect cybersecurity incidents

categories.name: Incident Management
categories.description: Responses to detected cybersecurity incidents are managed

categories.name: Incident Analysis
categories.description: Investigations are conducted to ensure effective response and support forensics and recovery activities

categories.name: Incident Response Reporting and Communication
categories.description: Response activities are coordinated with internal and external stakeholders as required by laws, regulations, or policies

categories.name: Incident Mitigation
categories.description: Activities are performed to prevent expansion of an event and mitigate its effects

categories.name: Incident Recovery Plan Execution
categories.description: Restoration activities are performed to ensure operational availability of systems and services affected by cybersecurity incidents

categories.name: Incident Recovery Communication
categories.description: Restoration activities are coordinated with internal and external parties

subcategories.name: GV.OC-01
subcategories.description: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Establish and communicate the organization's mission and objectives Ex2: Determine how cybersecurity risk management supports and enables the mission Ex3: Document the relationship between cybersecurity objectives and organizational objectives
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-11

subcategories.name: GV.OC-02
subcategories.description: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Identify relevant internal stakeholders and their cybersecurity-related expectations Ex2: Identify relevant external stakeholders and their cybersecurity-related expectations Ex3: Communicate with stakeholders to understand their needs
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-11, PM-25

subcategories.name: GV.OC-03
subcategories.description: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity — including privacy and civil liberties obligations — are understood and managed
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Determine legal and regulatory requirements affecting the organization Ex2: Determine contractual cybersecurity obligations Ex3: Integrate legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements into cybersecurity risk management
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-4, PM-6, PM-10

subcategories.name: GV.OC-04
subcategories.description: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Identify critical services the organization provides to external stakeholders Ex2: Determine stakeholder dependencies on organizational services Ex3: Communicate service-level expectations with stakeholders
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-11, PM-25

subcategories.name: GV.OC-05
subcategories.description: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Identify critical dependencies on external services and providers Ex2: Assess the cybersecurity posture of critical dependencies Ex3: Document and communicate dependency risks to leadership
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.1 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-11, SR-2

subcategories.name: GV.RM-01
subcategories.description: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Establish risk management objectives aligned with organizational mission Ex2: Obtain leadership agreement on risk management objectives Ex3: Communicate risk management objectives across the organization
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-9, PM-28

subcategories.name: GV.RM-02
subcategories.description: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Determine organizational risk appetite and tolerance levels Ex2: Document risk appetite and tolerance statements Ex3: Communicate risk appetite and tolerance to relevant stakeholders
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-9

subcategories.name: GV.RM-03
subcategories.description: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Integrate cybersecurity risk into enterprise risk management framework Ex2: Report cybersecurity risks alongside other enterprise risks Ex3: Align cybersecurity risk assessment methods with enterprise risk methods
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-9, PM-28

subcategories.name: GV.RM-04
subcategories.description: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Define acceptable risk response options (accept, avoid, mitigate, transfer) Ex2: Establish criteria for selecting risk response options Ex3: Communicate risk response guidance to operational teams
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-9

subcategories.name: GV.RM-05
subcategories.description: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Establish communication channels for cybersecurity risk information Ex2: Define escalation paths for cybersecurity risk issues Ex3: Include supply chain risk in communication protocols
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-9, PM-25, SR-1

subcategories.name: GV.RM-06
subcategories.description: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Adopt a standardized risk assessment methodology Ex2: Define risk categorization and prioritization criteria Ex3: Document and communicate the risk calculation method
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-9, RA-1, RA-3

subcategories.name: GV.RM-07
subcategories.description: Strategic opportunities (i.e., positive risks) are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Identify strategic opportunities from cybersecurity investments Ex2: Include positive risk scenarios in risk discussions Ex3: Evaluate cybersecurity improvements that enable business opportunities
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-9

subcategories.name: GV.RR-01
subcategories.description: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Leaders accept accountability for cybersecurity risk decisions Ex2: Foster a risk-aware organizational culture Ex3: Promote ethical behavior in cybersecurity practices
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-1, PM-2

subcategories.name: GV.RR-02
subcategories.description: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Define cybersecurity roles and responsibilities Ex2: Assign authorities for cybersecurity decisions Ex3: Communicate roles and responsibilities to all personnel
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-1, PM-2, PM-13

subcategories.name: GV.RR-03
subcategories.description: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Allocate budget for cybersecurity programs Ex2: Ensure adequate staffing for cybersecurity functions Ex3: Provide tools and technology resources for cybersecurity
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-3

subcategories.name: GV.RR-04
subcategories.description: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Include cybersecurity responsibilities in job descriptions Ex2: Conduct cybersecurity background checks for sensitive roles Ex3: Address cybersecurity in employee onboarding and offboarding
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PS-1, PS-2, PS-3, PS-4, PS-5

subcategories.name: GV.PO-01
subcategories.description: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Develop cybersecurity policy based on risk strategy Ex2: Communicate policy to all relevant personnel Ex3: Establish enforcement mechanisms for policy compliance
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: All -1 controls (policy families)

subcategories.name: GV.PO-02
subcategories.description: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Establish a policy review schedule Ex2: Update policies when significant changes occur Ex3: Communicate policy updates to affected personnel
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: All -1 controls (policy families)

subcategories.name: GV.OV-01
subcategories.description: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Review cybersecurity risk management outcomes periodically Ex2: Adjust strategy based on performance metrics Ex3: Report outcomes to leadership for decision-making
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-9, PM-31

subcategories.name: GV.OV-02
subcategories.description: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Assess strategy coverage against organizational requirements Ex2: Identify gaps in risk management coverage Ex3: Adjust strategy to address identified gaps
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-9, PM-28

subcategories.name: GV.OV-03
subcategories.description: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Define performance metrics for cybersecurity risk management Ex2: Evaluate performance against established metrics Ex3: Identify and implement needed adjustments
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-9, PM-14, PM-31

subcategories.name: GV.SC-01
subcategories.description: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Establish a supply chain risk management program Ex2: Define supply chain risk management objectives Ex3: Obtain stakeholder agreement on supply chain risk policies
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.1 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SR-1, SR-2, SR-3

subcategories.name: GV.SC-02
subcategories.description: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Define cybersecurity roles for suppliers and partners Ex2: Communicate expectations to third parties Ex3: Coordinate cybersecurity responsibilities across the supply chain
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.2 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SR-1, SR-2, SR-3, SR-5

subcategories.name: GV.SC-03
subcategories.description: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Integrate supply chain risk into enterprise risk assessments Ex2: Include supply chain considerations in improvement processes Ex3: Align supply chain risk management with overall cybersecurity strategy
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.1 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SR-1, SR-2, SR-3

subcategories.name: GV.SC-04
subcategories.description: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Maintain an inventory of suppliers Ex2: Assess supplier criticality based on dependency and risk Ex3: Prioritize supplier oversight based on criticality assessment
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.1, 15.3 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SR-2, SR-6

subcategories.name: GV.SC-05
subcategories.description: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Define cybersecurity requirements for supplier contracts Ex2: Prioritize requirements based on risk Ex3: Include cybersecurity clauses in all relevant agreements
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.2, 15.4 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SR-2, SR-3, SR-5

subcategories.name: GV.SC-06
subcategories.description: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Conduct due diligence assessments of potential suppliers Ex2: Evaluate supplier cybersecurity posture before engagement Ex3: Document risk acceptance decisions for supplier relationships
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.3, 15.4 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SR-3, SR-5, SR-6

subcategories.name: GV.SC-07
subcategories.description: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Continuously monitor supplier cybersecurity risks Ex2: Assess and record supplier risk changes Ex3: Respond to identified supplier risks appropriately
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.4, 15.5 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SR-3, SR-5, SR-6

subcategories.name: GV.SC-08
subcategories.description: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Include critical suppliers in incident response planning Ex2: Establish communication protocols with suppliers for incidents Ex3: Coordinate recovery activities with affected third parties
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.5, 17.1 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: IR-4, SR-8

subcategories.name: GV.SC-09
subcategories.description: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Integrate supply chain security into the product life cycle Ex2: Monitor supply chain security performance metrics Ex3: Review and improve supply chain practices regularly
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.1, 15.5 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SR-1, SR-2, SR-11

subcategories.name: GV.SC-10
subcategories.description: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Plan for data return or destruction at end of supplier relationship Ex2: Address access revocation upon contract termination Ex3: Document transition procedures for supplier changes
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.5 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SR-2, SR-3

subcategories.name: ID.AM-01
subcategories.description: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Maintain an inventory of all organizational hardware assets Ex2: Use automated tools to discover and catalog hardware Ex3: Regularly reconcile hardware inventory with physical assets
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 1.1, 1.2 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CM-8

subcategories.name: ID.AM-02
subcategories.description: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Maintain an inventory of all software and services Ex2: Use automated tools to discover installed software Ex3: Track software licenses and versions
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 2.1, 2.2 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CM-8

subcategories.name: ID.AM-03
subcategories.description: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Document authorized network communication flows Ex2: Maintain network architecture diagrams Ex3: Identify and document external data flows
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 12.2, 12.4 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: AC-4, CM-8

subcategories.name: ID.AM-04
subcategories.description: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Catalog all third-party services used by the organization Ex2: Document service dependencies and data flows Ex3: Track supplier service agreements and SLAs
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.1 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CM-8, SR-2

subcategories.name: ID.AM-05
subcategories.description: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact to the mission
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Classify assets based on data sensitivity and business impact Ex2: Prioritize assets for protection based on criticality Ex3: Allocate security resources based on asset priority
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 1.1, 2.1 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: RA-2, SC-6

subcategories.name: ID.AM-07
subcategories.description: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Maintain inventories of sensitive data and its locations Ex2: Catalog data types and their classification levels Ex3: Track data flows and storage locations
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 3.1, 3.2 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CM-8, CM-12, CM-13

subcategories.name: ID.AM-08
subcategories.description: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Implement asset lifecycle management processes Ex2: Track assets from acquisition through disposal Ex3: Ensure secure decommissioning of end-of-life assets
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 1.1, 2.1 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CM-8, SA-22

subcategories.name: ID.RA-01
subcategories.description: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Conduct regular vulnerability scans Ex2: Validate identified vulnerabilities Ex3: Record vulnerabilities in a tracking system
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.4 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CA-2, CA-8, RA-5, SI-4

subcategories.name: ID.RA-02
subcategories.description: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Subscribe to threat intelligence feeds Ex2: Participate in information sharing organizations Ex3: Integrate threat intelligence into risk assessments
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PM-16, RA-3, SI-5

subcategories.name: ID.RA-03
subcategories.description: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Identify potential internal threat sources Ex2: Identify potential external threat actors Ex3: Document and categorize identified threats
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: RA-3, PM-12, PM-16

subcategories.name: ID.RA-04
subcategories.description: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Assess likelihood of threat exploitation Ex2: Determine potential business impact of exploitation Ex3: Document risk scenarios with impact and likelihood ratings
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: RA-3, RA-5

subcategories.name: ID.RA-05
subcategories.description: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Calculate inherent risk from threat and vulnerability data Ex2: Prioritize risk responses based on risk levels Ex3: Document risk response decisions and rationale
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: RA-3, PM-9

subcategories.name: ID.RA-06
subcategories.description: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Select appropriate risk response for each identified risk Ex2: Develop and track risk response plans Ex3: Communicate risk response status to stakeholders
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: RA-7, PM-4

subcategories.name: ID.RA-07
subcategories.description: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Assess cybersecurity risk impact of proposed changes Ex2: Document and track risk exceptions Ex3: Review exceptions periodically for continued validity
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CA-7, CM-3, CM-4

subcategories.name: ID.RA-08
subcategories.description: Processes for receiving, analyzing, and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Establish a vulnerability disclosure program Ex2: Define processes for analyzing disclosed vulnerabilities Ex3: Implement response procedures for vulnerability disclosures
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 7.5 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: RA-5, SI-2, SI-5

subcategories.name: ID.RA-09
subcategories.description: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Verify software integrity before installation Ex2: Validate hardware authenticity from suppliers Ex3: Use trusted sources for software acquisition
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 2.3, 2.5 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: RA-3, SR-4, SR-11

subcategories.name: ID.RA-10
subcategories.description: Critical suppliers are assessed prior to acquisition
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Conduct security assessments of critical suppliers Ex2: Evaluate supplier security certifications and practices Ex3: Include security criteria in supplier selection process
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 15.3, 15.4 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: RA-3, SR-3, SR-5, SR-6

subcategories.name: ID.IM-01
subcategories.description: Improvements are identified from evaluations
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Conduct periodic evaluations of cybersecurity processes Ex2: Identify improvement opportunities from evaluation results Ex3: Document and prioritize identified improvements
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CA-2, CA-7, PM-4, PM-14

subcategories.name: ID.IM-02
subcategories.description: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Conduct regular security testing and exercises Ex2: Include suppliers in security exercises Ex3: Document lessons learned and improvement actions
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 17.1, 17.6 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CA-2, CA-8, CP-4, IR-3

subcategories.name: ID.IM-03
subcategories.description: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Review operational processes for cybersecurity improvements Ex2: Collect feedback from operational teams Ex3: Implement process improvements based on operational experience
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CA-2, CA-7, PM-4

subcategories.name: ID.IM-04
subcategories.description: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Develop and maintain incident response plans Ex2: Communicate plans to relevant personnel Ex3: Improve plans based on lessons learned from incidents and exercises
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 17.4 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CP-2, IR-8, PM-8

subcategories.name: PR.AA-01
subcategories.description: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Implement identity lifecycle management processes Ex2: Manage credentials including issuance, rotation, and revocation Ex3: Maintain identity records for all authorized entities
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: IA-1, IA-2, IA-3, IA-4, IA-5, IA-8

subcategories.name: PR.AA-02
subcategories.description: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Implement identity proofing procedures appropriate to risk level Ex2: Bind verified identities to issued credentials Ex3: Verify identity before granting access to sensitive resources
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 5.1, 5.2 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: IA-1, IA-2, IA-5, IA-12

subcategories.name: PR.AA-03
subcategories.description: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Implement multi-factor authentication for privileged access Ex2: Authenticate all users before granting system access Ex3: Implement device authentication for network access
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 5.2, 5.4, 6.3, 6.4, 6.5 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: IA-2, IA-3, IA-8, IA-9

subcategories.name: PR.AA-04
subcategories.description: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Protect identity assertions during transmission Ex2: Verify identity assertions before granting access Ex3: Implement secure token management for identity assertions
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 5.6 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: IA-2, IA-5, SC-12, SC-13

subcategories.name: PR.AA-05
subcategories.description: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Define access control policies based on least privilege Ex2: Implement separation of duties for critical functions Ex3: Review and recertify access permissions periodically
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 3.3, 5.4, 6.1, 6.2, 6.8 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-6, AC-24

subcategories.name: PR.AA-06
subcategories.description: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Implement physical access controls for sensitive areas Ex2: Monitor physical access to critical assets Ex3: Review and update physical access authorizations
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 0 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: PE-1, PE-2, PE-3, PE-4, PE-5, PE-6

subcategories.name: PR.AT-01
subcategories.description: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Conduct regular cybersecurity awareness training for all personnel Ex2: Include cybersecurity topics in new employee orientation Ex3: Test awareness through simulated phishing exercises
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 14.1, 14.2, 14.3 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: AT-1, AT-2, AT-3, AT-4

subcategories.name: PR.AT-02
subcategories.description: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Provide role-specific cybersecurity training for IT staff Ex2: Train developers on secure coding practices Ex3: Provide incident response training for security team members
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 14.9 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: AT-2, AT-3, AT-4

subcategories.name: PR.DS-01
subcategories.description: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Encrypt sensitive data at rest Ex2: Implement access controls for stored data Ex3: Use integrity verification for critical data stores
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 3.6, 3.7, 3.11 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SC-28

subcategories.name: PR.DS-02
subcategories.description: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected
subcategories.implementationExamples: Ex1: Encrypt data in transit using TLS/SSL Ex2: Implement VPN for remote access communications Ex3: Verify data integrity during transmission
subcategories.informativeReferences: CIS Controls v8: 3.10 | NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SC-8, SC-13

subcategories.name: PR.DS-10
